contents.name: Box 2: helicity-dependent phase from rotations of transverse coordinates
contents.support: The review describes opposite phases for the two circular helicities under rotation. The item states the active rotation convention and derives its exact e^{-i sigma alpha} sign from the local eigenframe; the review's per-photon hbar=1 language is not adopted as a quantum premise.

contents.name: Box 2: transverse polarization transported on the sphere of wavevector directions
contents.support: The source identifies the direction sphere and the polarization dependence on the wavevector. The item defines the classical rank-one projector bundle directly from the current helicity-projection supplier and does not use a photon position operator.

contents.name: Box 2: Berry connection, curvature, and phase along a direction contour
contents.support: The source gives the optical geometric-phase context. The local proof calculates the sign, smooth global area-form expression, flux, and no-global-frame obstruction without relying on the review as a proof.

contents.name: Box 2: closed contour on the direction sphere gives opposite helicity phases
contents.support: The example computes one finite latitude loop from the proved local connection and compares its two gauges; it asserts no experiment or empirical phase measurement.

contents.name: §1.5.1: Abelian Berry phase from parallel transport along a closed parameter path
contents.support: The lecture derives a connection integral from its adiabatic quantum model. The local classical proof derives the projected-connection ODE explicitly and assumes no adiabatic theorem or Hamiltonian.

contents.name: §1.5.1: phase-gauge change, curvature, and a surface expression using Stokes
contents.support: The notes explain the local phase redundancy and gauge-invariant curvature. Their convention A=-i<n|dn> is opposite to this item's A=i v-dagger d v; the item derives its own transformation sign and cites exact mathematical suppliers.

contents.name: §1.5.2: spin-in-a-field local eigenstates, monopole curvature, flux, and solid-angle phase
contents.support: This is a spin-1/2 quantum example with a level-crossing point. The new proof is for the classical spin-1 helicity line and computes its flux directly; no quantum Hamiltonian, adiabatic condition, or monopole source is imported.

contents.name: §1.5.2: alternate spanning surfaces and the phase ambiguity resolved by quantized curvature flux
contents.reason: The alternate-surface argument in Tong is for a spin-1/2 quantum Hamiltonian with an adiabatic level crossing; this page proves the classical helicity flux directly and does not import that quantum model.
